metadata.legislation: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022
metadata.jurisdiction: Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
metadata.description: Structured PDPA requirements for AI-assisted compliance analysis. Each entry maps to one numbered subsection of the Act. Schedules are folded into their parent sections.

requirements.clause_title: Compliance with the Data Protection Obligations
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall process personal data in compliance with the obligations specified under this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Process Personal Data in a Lawful Manner
requirements.requirement: Processing is lawful only if the controller is in compliance with at least one condition in Schedule I (general data), or at least one condition in Schedule II (special categories of personal data), or all conditions of Schedule III (when consent is the basis under Schedule I(a) or Schedule II(a)), or all conditions of Schedule IV (criminal investigations).

Schedule_I.description: Conditions for Lawful Processing (general personal data)
conditions: (a) the data subject has given consent to the processing of his personal data
(b) processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is a party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract
(c) processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller or processor is subject to under any written law
(d) processing is necessary to respond to an emergency that threatens the life, health or safety of the data subject or another natural person

(e) processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of powers, functions or duties conferred, imposed or assigned on the controller or processor by or under any written law including any circular, direction or code issued by the government

(f) processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party, except where such interests are overridden by the interests of the data subject which require protection of personal data, in particular where the data subject is a child

(g) [definition of public interest for item (e)] — includes: (i) processing necessary for health purposes such as public health and social protection and the management of health care services; (ii) processing necessary for the control of communicable diseases and other serious threats to health; (iii) processing by official authorities for achieving the purposes or objects laid down by law

(h) [definition of legitimate interest for item (f)] — includes: (i) processing in situations where the data subject is a client or in the service of a controller; (ii) whether a data subject reasonably expects at the time and in the context of the collection of the personal data that processing for that purpose may take place; (iii) processing strictly necessary for the purposes of preventing fraud; (iv) processing to the extent strictly necessary and proportionate for the purposes of ensuring network and information security

Schedule_II.description: Conditions for Processing Special Categories of Personal Data
conditions: (a) the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of special categories of personal data for one or more purposes specified by the controller at the time of processing, unless any other written law prohibits processing notwithstanding consent. In the case of a child, consent shall mean the consent of the parent or legal guardian

(b) processing is necessary for the purposes of carrying out the obligations of the controller and exercising of the rights of the data subject in the field of employment, social security including pension, and for public health purposes ensuring public safety, monitoring and public alert systems relating to impending health or other emergencies, the prevention or control of communicable diseases and other serious threats to public health and the management of public healthcare services, in so far as it is provided for in any written law providing for appropriate safeguards for rights of the data subject

(c) processing is necessary to respond to an emergency that threatens the life, health or safety of the data subject or another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent
(d) processing relates to personal data which is manifestly made public by the data subject
(e) processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims before a court or tribunal or such similar forum, or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity

(f) processing is necessary for any purpose as provided for in any written law or public interest as determined under item (g) of Schedule I, which shall be necessary and proportionate to the aim pursued whilst providing suitable and specific measures to safeguard the rights and freedoms of the data subject

(g) processing is necessary for the purposes of preventive or occupational medicine, medical diagnosis, the provision of care or treatment or the management of health-care services, and where such data is processed by a health professional licensed under or authorized by any written law prevailing in Sri Lanka

(h) processing is necessary for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific research or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with law which shall be proportionate to the aim pursued, protecting the data protection rights enumerated in this Act or any other written law and provide for suitable and specific measures to safeguard the rights and freedoms of the data subject

Schedule_III.description: Conditions for Consent of the Data Subject
conditions: (a) the controller shall demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of the personal data relating to such data subject

(b) if the consent of the data subject is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language; such a declaration shall not constitute an infringement of any provisions of this Act

(c) when assessing whether consent is freely given, special consideration shall be taken of whether the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract
(d) prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed that consent can be withdrawn at any time subject to the provisions of this Act

Schedule_IV.description: Processing of Personal Data Relating to Criminal Investigations
conditions: (a) processing of personal data relating to lawful investigations of offences or related security measures shall be carried out only in accordance with applicable written laws, whilst providing for appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of data subjects

(b) for the avoidance of doubt, processing of personal data may be considered lawful under this Schedule if investigations are carried out pursuant to the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 or provisions under any other written law
(c) conditions for providing appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of data subjects under this Schedule may be as prescribed

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Define a Purpose — Purpose Specification
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall ensure that personal data is processed for purposes that are (a) specified, (b) explicit, and (c) legitimate. Personal data shall not be further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Define a Purpose — Archiving and Research Exception
requirements.requirement: Subject to section 10, further processing of personal data by a controller for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific research, historical research, or statistical purposes shall not be considered to be incompatible with the initial specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes referred to in section 6(1).

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Confine Personal Data Processing to the Defined Purpose — Data Minimisation
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall ensure that personal data that is processed shall be (a) adequate, (b) relevant, and (c) proportionate, to the extent as is necessary in relation to the purpose for which such data shall be collected or processed.

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Ensure Accuracy
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall ensure that personal data that is processed shall be (a) accurate and (b) kept up to date, with every reasonable step being taken to erase or rectify any inaccurate or outdated personal data without undue delay.

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Limit the Period of Retention — Storage Limitation
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall ensure that personal data that is being processed shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects only for such period as may be necessary or required for the purposes for which such personal data is processed. Subject to section 10, a controller may store personal data for longer periods in so far as the personal data shall be processed further for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific research, historical research, or statistical purposes.

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Maintain Integrity and Confidentiality — Security
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall ensure integrity and confidentiality of personal data that is being processed by using appropriate technical and organizational measures including encryption, pseudonymisation, anonymisation, or access controls, or such other measures as may be prescribed, so as to prevent: (a) unauthorized or unlawful processing of personal data, or (b) loss, destruction, or damage of personal data.

requirements.clause_title: Obligation to Process Personal Data in a Transparent Manner
requirements.requirement: A controller shall provide data subjects (a) the information referred to in Schedule V, and (b) the information regarding any decision taken pursuant to a request made under Part II of this Act, in writing or by electronic means and in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form.

Schedule_V.description: Collection of Personal Data — Information to be Provided to Data Subjects

items.description: Where personal data is collected from the data subject, the controller shall provide the following at the time of collection
sub_items: (a) the identity and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the controller's representative
(b) the contact details of the Data Protection Officer, where applicable
(c) the intended purposes for which the personal data is processed and the legal basis for the processing
(d) the legitimate interest pursued by the controller or by a third party where processing is based on Schedule I item (f)
(e) the categories of personal data being collected

(f) where processing is based on consent under Schedule I(a) or Schedule II(a), the existence of the right to withdraw consent and the procedure for such withdrawal, without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal
(g) recipients or third parties with whom such personal data may be shared, if applicable
(h) information regarding any cross-border transfer of the personal data that the controller intends to carry out, if applicable
(i) the period for which personal data shall be retained under section 9, or where such period is not known, the criteria for determining such period
(j) the existence of and procedure for the exercise of data subject rights referred to in Part II
(k) the existence of a right to file complaints to the Authority

(l) whether the provision of personal data is a statutory or contractual requirement, or a requirement necessary to enter into a contract, as well as whether the data subject is obliged to provide personal data and the possible consequences of failure to do so

(m) the existence of automated individual decision-making under section 18, including profiling, and at least in those cases, reasonably meaningful information about the logic involved, as well as the significance and the envisaged consequences of such processing for the data subject

items.description: Where the controller intends to further process the personal data for a purpose other than for which it was originally collected, the controller shall provide the data subject with detailed information on the further processing and the purpose thereof in the same manner as item 1
Items 1 and 2 shall not apply where the data subject already has obtained or been made aware of the information

Where personal data has been obtained other than through direct interaction with the data subject, the controller shall also provide the source from which the personal data originates, and whether it came from a publicly accessible source, in addition to the information in item 1

Where personal data is obtained other than through direct interaction, the information under items 1 and 4 shall be provided: (a) within a reasonable period after obtaining the data, but at least within one month; (b) if used for communication with the data subject, at least at the time of the first communication; or (c) if a disclosure to another recipient is envisaged, at least when the personal data is first disclosed

Items 1 to 4 shall not apply where: (a) the data subject already has the information; (b) provision would be impossible or involve disproportionate effort, particularly for archiving, scientific, historical, or statistical research purposes subject to applicable conditions and safeguards — in such cases the controller shall take appropriate measures to protect data subject rights including making relevant information publicly available; (c) obtaining or disclosure is expressly laid down by any written law which provides appropriate measures to protect data subject rights; or (d) the personal data shall remain confidential due to professional privilege or is not permitted to be disclosed under any written law including a statutory obligation of secrecy

requirements.clause_title: Accountability in the Processing of Personal Data — Data Protection Management Programme
requirements.requirement: Every controller shall implement internal controls and procedures (the 'Data Protection Management Programme') that: (a) establishes and maintains duly catalogued records to demonstrate implementation of data protection obligations under sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11; (b) is designed on the basis of structure, scale, volume, and sensitivity of processing activities; (c) provides for appropriate safeguards based on data protection impact assessments under section 24; (d) is integrated into the governance structure of the controller; (e) establishes internal oversight mechanisms; (f) has a mechanism to receive complaints, conduct inquiries, and identify personal data breaches; (g) is updated based on periodic monitoring and assessments; and (h) facilitates the exercise of data subject rights under sections 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18.

requirements.clause_title: Accountability — Authority Guidelines on Data Protection Management Programme
requirements.requirement: The Authority shall from time to time issue such guidelines in respect of the Data Protection Management Programme.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Access to Personal Data — Data Subject's Right
requirements.requirement: Every data subject shall have the right to access personal data relating to such data subject and to be provided with a confirmation as to whether such personal data has been processed and such information referred to in Schedule V, upon a written request made by such data subject to the controller.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Access to Personal Data — Controller's Obligation to Respond
requirements.requirement: The controller shall, upon receipt of a written request made by the data subject under section 13(1), provide the data subject with such information required to be provided under Schedule V, subject to the provisions of section 17.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Withdrawal of Consent
requirements.requirement: Every data subject shall have the right to withdraw consent at any time upon a written request made to the controller if processing is based on consent under Schedule I(a) or Schedule II(a). The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of any processing that took place prior to such withdrawal.

requirements.clause_title: Right to Object to Processing
requirements.requirement: Every data subject shall have the right to request a controller in writing to refrain from further processing of personal data relating to such data subject, if such processing is based on the grounds specified in Schedule I(e) or Schedule I(f) or Schedule II(f).

requirements.clause_title: Right to Rectification or Completion
requirements.requirement: Every data subject shall have the right to request a controller in writing to rectify or complete personal data relating to such data subject which is either inaccurate or incomplete. The controller shall, upon such written request, rectify or complete the personal data without undue delay subject to section 17. This section shall not impose any obligation on a controller to collect and process additional personal data not required for the processing purpose. Where a controller is required to maintain personal data for evidentiary purposes under any written law or court order, the controller shall refrain from further processing such personal data without rectifying it.

requirements.clause_title: Right to Erasure
requirements.requirement: Every data subject shall have the right to make a written request to the controller to have personal data erased under the following circumstances: (a) the processing of personal data is carried out in contravention of the obligations referred to in sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11; (b) the data subject withdraws consent upon which the processing is based, in accordance with Schedule I(a) or Schedule II(a); or (c) the requirement to erase personal data is required by any written law or on an order of a competent court to which the data subject or controller is subject.

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Response Timeline and Content
requirements.requirement: Where a controller receives a written request from a data subject under sections 13, 14, 15 or 16, the controller shall inform the data subject in writing within twenty-one working days from the date of such request, whether: (a) such request has been granted; (b) such request has been refused under section 17(2) and the reasons thereof unless such disclosure is prohibited by any written law; or (c) the controller has refrained from further processing under sections 14(2) or 15 and reasons thereof. The controller must also inform the data subject of the availability of the right of appeal in respect of decisions made under paragraphs (b) or (c).

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Grounds for Refusal
requirements.requirement: The controller may refuse to act on a request made under sections 13, 14, 15 or 16 by a data subject having regard to: (a) national security; (b) public order; (c) any inquiry, investigation, or procedure carried out under any written law; (d) the prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of criminal offences; (e) the rights and freedoms of other persons under any written law; (f) subject to section 17(4), the technical and operational feasibility of the controller to act on such request; (g) subject to section 17(4), the inability of the controller to establish the identity of the data subject; or (h) the requirement to process personal data under any written law.

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Recording of Refusals
requirements.requirement: A controller shall record the reasons for any refusal under section 17(2) and submit such records to the Authority upon a written request from the Authority.

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Identity Verification
requirements.requirement: Where a controller is unable to establish the identity of a data subject making a request under sections 13, 14, 15 or 16, such controller may request the data subject to provide additional information to enable the controller to carry out such requests.

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Exercise of Rights by Proxy
requirements.requirement: Any right conferred on a data subject under Part II may be exercised: (a) where the data subject is a minor, by parents or a person who has parental authority or has been appointed as legal guardian; (b) where the data subject is physically or mentally unfit, by a person appointed as guardian or administrator by a court; (c) by a person duly authorised in writing by the data subject, except in cases covered by (a) and (b); or (d) by an heir to exercise a deceased data subject's rights within ten years from the date of the data subject's demise, in the manner prescribed by regulations.

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Fees for Requests
requirements.requirement: A request made by a data subject under sections 13, 14, 15 or 16 may be accompanied by such fees as may be prescribed by regulations made under this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Grant or Refusal of Data Subject Requests — Fee Notification
requirements.requirement: Where a fee is charged under section 17(6), the controller shall inform the data subject of the details of such fees and the reasons for imposing them.

requirements.clause_title: Automated Individual Decision Making — Right to Request Review
requirements.requirement: Subject to section 19, every data subject shall have the right to request a controller to review a decision of such controller based solely on automated processing, which has created or is likely to create an irreversible and continuous impact on the rights and freedoms of the data subject under any written law.

requirements.clause_title: Automated Individual Decision Making — Exceptions
requirements.requirement: Section 18(1) shall not apply where a decision based on automated processing is: (a) authorized by any written law applicable to the controller; (b) authorized in a manner determined by the Authority; (c) based on the consent of the data subject; or (d) necessary for entering into or performance of a contract between the data subject and the controller. In cases (a)–(d), the controller shall comply with such measures and applicable criteria as may be specified by the Authority to safeguard the rights and freedoms of the data subject. The exception under paragraph (d) shall not apply to special categories of personal data.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Appeal of Data Subjects to the Authority — Circumstances of Appeal
requirements.requirement: Where a controller: (a) has not refrained from further processing under section 14; (b) has refused to rectify or complete personal data under section 15; (c) has refused to erase personal data under section 16; (d) has refused the request of the data subject under section 17(2); or (e) has refused the request to review an automated decision under section 18(1), the data subject may appeal against such decision in the form, manner and within such period of time as may be prescribed.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Appeal — Authority's Determination
requirements.requirement: The Authority may determine whether the: (a) decision not to refrain from further processing under section 14 was lawful; (b) decision to refuse to rectify or complete personal data under section 15 was lawful; (c) decision to refuse erasure under section 16 was lawful; (d) refusal under section 17(2) was lawful; or (e) refusal to review an automated decision under section 18(1) was lawful.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Appeal — Timeline and Communication of Determination
requirements.requirement: After concluding the necessary investigations, the Authority shall determine within such period as may be prescribed whether the appeal is allowed or disallowed, and the Authority shall inform both the data subject and the controller of the determination with reasons thereof.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Appeal — Implementation of Authority Decision by Controller
requirements.requirement: Where the Authority allows the appeal, the controller shall take steps to give effect to the decision of the Authority within such period as may be determined by the Authority, and the controller shall inform both the data subject and the Authority of the steps taken to give effect to its decision.

requirements.clause_title: Right of Appeal — Further Appeal to Court of Appeal
requirements.requirement: Any data subject or controller aggrieved by the decision of the Authority may prefer an appeal to the Court of Appeal not later than thirty days from the date of such decision.

requirements.clause_title: Designation or Appointment of the Data Protection Officer — Mandatory Circumstances
requirements.requirement: Every controller and processor shall designate or appoint a Data Protection Officer to ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act in the following circumstances: (a) where the processing is carried out by a ministry, government department or public corporation, except for the judiciary acting in their judicial capacity; or (b) where the core activities consist of: (i) operations requiring regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a scale and magnitude as may be prescribed; or (ii) processing of special categories of personal data on a scale and magnitude as may be prescribed; or (iii) processing which results in a risk of harm affecting the rights of data subjects based on the nature of processing and its impact on data subjects.

requirements.clause_title: Data Protection Officer — Qualifications
requirements.requirement: A Data Protection Officer shall possess relevant academic and professional qualifications as may be prescribed, which may include academic background, knowledge and technical skills in matters relating to data protection, with competency and capacity to implement strategies and mechanisms to respond to inquiries and incidents related to processing of personal data.

requirements.clause_title: Data Protection Officer — Group of Entities and Public Authorities
requirements.requirement: Where the controller is a group of entities, such controller may appoint a single Data Protection Officer who is easily accessible by each entity. Where a controller or processor is a public authority, a single Data Protection Officer may be designated for several such public authorities, taking into account their organisational structures.

requirements.clause_title: Data Protection Officer — Publication of Contact Details
requirements.requirement: A controller or processor shall publish the contact details of the Data Protection Officer and communicate such details to the Authority.

requirements.clause_title: Data Protection Officer — Responsibilities
requirements.requirement: The responsibility of the Data Protection Officer shall be to: (a) advise the controller or processor and their employees on data processing requirements under this Act or any other written law; (b) ensure on behalf of the controller or processor that the provisions of this Act are complied with; (c) facilitate capacity building of staff involved in data processing operations; (d) provide advice on personal data protection impact assessments; and (e) co-operate and comply with all directives and instructions issued by the Authority on matters relating to data protection.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of a Controller — Processor Selection and Contract
requirements.requirement: Where processing is to be carried out by a processor on behalf of a controller, the controller shall: (a) use only processors who ensure the provision of appropriate technical and organisational measures to give effect to the provisions of this Act and ensure the protection of rights of the data subjects; and (b) ensure that such processor is bound by a contract or provisions of any written law which sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of the data subjects, and the obligations of the controller.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of a Controller — Joint Controllers
requirements.requirement: Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing, such controllers shall be referred to as 'joint controllers' who shall be jointly responsible for discharging the obligations stipulated under this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of the Processors — Core Processor Obligations
requirements.requirement: Where a processor is engaged in processing activities on behalf of the controller, the processor shall: (a) ensure that processing activities are carried out only on the written instructions of the controller; (b) ensure that its personnel are bound by contractual obligations on confidentiality and secrecy by implementing appropriate technical and organisational measures; (c) facilitate the controller to carry out compliance audits, including inspections, upon the written request of the controller, taking into account the nature of processing and information available to the processor; and (d) upon the written instructions of the controller, erase existing copies of personal data or return all personal data to the controller after the completion of services relating to processing.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of the Processors — Processor Deemed Controller
requirements.requirement: Where a processor fails to comply with section 22(1)(a) or determines the purposes and means of processing by itself, such processor shall, for the purposes of this Act, be deemed to be a controller in respect of such processing.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of the Processors — Sub-Processors
requirements.requirement: Where a processor engages another processor (sub-processor) for carrying out specific processing activities, the provisions of section 22 shall apply to and in relation to such sub-processor.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of the Processors — Sub-Processor Liability
requirements.requirement: Where a sub-processor fails to fulfil its obligations under section 22(3), the processor shall be liable to the controller for the performance or carrying out of the obligations of such sub-processor.

requirements.clause_title: Additional Obligations of the Processors — Definition of Personnel
requirements.requirement: For the purposes of section 22, 'personnel' means any employee, consultant, agent, affiliate, or any person who is contracted by the processor to process personal data.

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Breach Notifications — Controller's Obligation to Notify Authority
requirements.requirement: In the event of a personal data breach, a controller shall notify the Authority regarding such personal data breach in such form, manner, and within such period of time as may be determined by rules made under this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Breach Notifications — Authority Rules on Breach Notification
requirements.requirement: The Authority shall provide for: (a) the circumstances where the Authority shall be notified of a data breach; (b) the circumstances where the affected data subject shall be notified; and (c) the form and manner of making such notification and the information which shall be provided in such notification relating to the data breach, by way of rules made under this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments — When a DPIA is Required
requirements.requirement: Where a controller intends to carry out any processing which involves: (a) a systematic and extensive evaluation of personal data or special categories of personal data including profiling; (b) a systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas or telecommunication networks; or (c) a processing activity as may be determined by rules taking into consideration the scope and associated risks of that processing, such controller shall, prior to such processing, carry out a personal data protection impact assessment (DPIA) in a form and manner as may be prescribed, to ascertain the impact of the intended processing on the obligations imposed on the controller under Part I of this Act and the rights of data subjects under Part II of this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments — DPIA Content
requirements.requirement: The personal data protection impact assessment shall contain such information and particulars including any measures and safeguards taken by the controller to mitigate any risk of harm caused to the data subject by the processing referred to in section 24(1).

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments — DPO Assistance
requirements.requirement: The controller shall seek the assistance of the Data Protection Officer, where designated, when carrying out a personal data protection impact assessment under section 24(1).

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments — Fresh DPIA on Process Changes
requirements.requirement: The controller shall conduct a fresh personal data protection impact assessment in accordance with section 24 whenever there is any change in the methodology, technology, or process adopted in the processing for which a DPIA has already been carried out.

requirements.clause_title: Personal Data Protection Impact Assessments — Submission to Authority
requirements.requirement: The controller shall submit to the Authority the personal data protection impact assessment required under section 24 and, on written request made by the Authority, provide any other information for the purpose of making an assessment on the compliance of the processing and in respect of any risks of harm associated with the protection of personal data of the data subject and of the related safeguards recommended by the Authority.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Mitigation Before Processing
requirements.requirement: Where a personal data protection impact assessment carried out under section 24 indicates that the processing is likely to result in a risk of harm to the rights of the data subjects guaranteed under this Act or any written law, a controller shall take such measures to mitigate such risk of harm, prior to any processing of personal data.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Consultation with Authority
requirements.requirement: Where a controller, despite having taken measures under section 25(1), is not able to mitigate such risks of harm to the data subject, such controller may consult the Authority prior to such processing.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Authority Instructions
requirements.requirement: Upon such consultation, the Authority may issue written instructions to the controller requiring it to take additional measures to mitigate any risk of harm to the data subject or to cease such processing.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Additional Information to Authority
requirements.requirement: Where the controller consults the Authority under section 25(2), the controller shall provide additional information as may be requested by the Authority.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Non-Compliance with Authority Instructions
requirements.requirement: Where the controller fails to comply with the instructions of the Authority without any reasonable cause, such controller shall contravene the provisions of this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Deemed Safeguards for Schedule II Processing
requirements.requirement: For the avoidance of doubt, when processing of personal data referred to in Schedule II items (b), (f), (g) and (h) is undertaken, such processing shall be considered to have provided such measures and appropriate safeguards to protect the rights of the data subjects required under Schedule II.

requirements.clause_title: Measures to Mitigate Risks of Harm and Prior Consultation — Mandatory Consultation for National Security, Public Order and Public Health Processing
requirements.requirement: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in any other written law, whenever the controller engages in processing of personal data referred to in section 24(1) and where such processing is carried out by a controller in relation to national security, public order, and public health, the controller shall consult the Authority.

requirements.clause_title: Cross-Border Data Flow — Data Localisation for Public Authorities
requirements.requirement: Where a public authority processes personal data as a controller or processor, such personal data shall be processed only in Sri Lanka and shall not be processed in a third country, unless the Authority in consultation with that controller or processor and the relevant regulatory or statutory body classifies the categories of personal data which may be permitted to be processed in a third country prescribed by the Minister pursuant to an adequacy decision under section 26(2).

requirements.clause_title: Cross-Border Data Flow — Adequacy Decision
requirements.requirement: For the purpose of making an adequacy decision, the Minister shall, in consultation with the Authority, take into consideration: the relevant written law and enforcement mechanisms relating to the protection of personal data in a third country; the application of Parts I, II and sections 20–25 of Part III; and such other prescribed criteria relating to the processing of personal data in a third country. Any adequacy decision: (i) shall be subject to periodic monitoring of developments in the third country that may affect such decisions, and the Minister may review such decision at least every two years; and (ii) shall remain in force until amended or revoked by the Minister in consultation with the Authority.

requirements.clause_title: Cross-Border Data Flow — Transfer Options for Non-Public Authority Controllers and Processors
requirements.requirement: A controller or processor other than a public authority may process personal data: (a) in a third country prescribed pursuant to an adequacy decision; or (b) in a country not covered by an adequacy decision, only where such controller or processor ensures compliance with the respective obligations imposed under Parts I, II and sections 20–25 of Part III of this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Cross-Border Data Flow — Appropriate Safeguards Instruments
requirements.requirement: For the purpose of ensuring compliance under section 26(3)(b), a controller or processor shall adopt such instruments as may be specified by the Authority to ensure binding and enforceable commitments of the recipient in the third country to ensure appropriate safeguards to the rights of the data subjects and remedies protected by this Act.

requirements.clause_title: Cross-Border Data Flow — Derogations in the Absence of Adequacy Decision or Appropriate Safeguards
requirements.requirement: In the absence of an adequacy decision under section 26(2) or appropriate safeguards under section 26(4), a controller or processor other than a public authority may process personal data outside Sri Lanka if: (a) the data subject has explicitly consented to the proposed processing outside Sri Lanka, after having been informed of the possible risks due to absence of adequacy decision and appropriate safeguards; (b) the transfer is necessary for the performance of a contract between the data subject and the controller or the implementation of pre-contractual measures taken at the request of the data subject; (c) the transfer is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims relating to the data subject; (d) the transfer is necessary for reasons of public interest as defined in Schedule I(g); (e) the transfer is necessary to respond to an emergency threatening the life, health, or safety of the data subject or another person where the data subject or legal guardian is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or (f) such processing is permitted under any other conditions as may be prescribed under this Act.

requirements.part_title: Use of Personal Data to Disseminate Solicited Messages
requirements.clause_title: Solicited Messages to Data Subjects — Consent Requirement
requirements.requirement: Subject to section 14, a controller may use postal services, telecommunication services, electronic means, or any other similar means for the purposes of disseminating messages only if a data subject has given consent to receive such messages (solicited messages).

requirements.part_title: Use of Personal Data to Disseminate Solicited Messages
requirements.clause_title: Solicited Messages — Conditions for Consent
requirements.requirement: For the purpose of section 27(1), consent shall be obtained by a controller in accordance with the conditions of Schedule III of this Act.

requirements.part_title: Use of Personal Data to Disseminate Solicited Messages
requirements.clause_title: Solicited Messages — Opt-Out Mechanism
requirements.requirement: When obtaining consent under section 27(1), the controller shall, at the time of collecting contact information and each time where a message is sent, provide to the data subject details on how to opt-out of receiving solicited messages free of charge.

requirements.part_title: Use of Personal Data to Disseminate Solicited Messages
requirements.clause_title: Solicited Messages — Identity Disclosure Obligation
requirements.requirement: A controller using postal, electronic, telecommunication, or any other similar means to disseminate any solicited message shall inform the data subjects, to whom such messages are intended, of the nature of the message and the identity of the controller or third party on behalf of whom the message is disseminated by the controller.

requirements.part_title: Use of Personal Data to Disseminate Solicited Messages
requirements.clause_title: Solicited Messages — Authority Codes and Prefixes
requirements.requirement: The Authority may, in consultation with the relevant regulatory or statutory body, determine by way of rules made under this Act any code or prefix that controllers shall adopt in order to identify different categories of solicited messages.

requirements.part_title: Use of Personal Data to Disseminate Solicited Messages
requirements.clause_title: Solicited Messages — Definition of Message
requirements.requirement: For the purpose of section 27, a 'message' includes any written, electronic, oral, pictorial, or video message that is intended to promote: (a) goods or services of a controller or any third party; or (b) any person, entity or organisation including the controller, using postal, electronic or telecommunication services or any other similar methods, including the use of automated calling and communication systems with or without human intervention, other than any internet-based advertisements to which a data subject has consented to obtain a service free of charge from the controller.
